NEW DELHI: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged unilateral decisions taken in connection with the Election Commission (ECI) electoral roll revision exercise, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. The petitioner has also sought a Special Investigation Team (SIT) inquiry into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls.The plea seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners are illegal and calls for restoration of the original Form 6 used for voter registration. It also seeks prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar, deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI IT head Seema Khanna for alleged violations of duties under the Representation of the People Act.The petition follows a report by The Indian Express stating that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions concerning the addition, deletion and restoration of voters and changes to the voter registration process.The petitioner has sought prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act.EC has maintained that all decisions, including those relating to SIR, were unanimous and taken with the approval of both Election Commissioners and the CEC.
Article Summary: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar. The plea seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners are illegal. The petition also seeks a Special Investigation Team (SIT) inquiry into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls.

NEW DELHI: India on Thursday rebuked Pakistan over its remarks on Kashmir and minorities in India at the UN Human Rights Council, calling out Islamabad for its illegal occupation of parts of Jammu and Kashmir and demanding that it vacate them.Exercising India's right to reply to the comments made by Pakistan at the council, Indian diplomat Kshitij Tyagi advised Islamabad to direct its energy towards a debt-ridden economy surviving on bailouts rather than harbouring territorial ambitions or sponsoring cross-border terrorism."Since Pakistan appears to need the reminder under every agenda item, Jammu and Kashmir was, is and will always remain an integral and inalienable part of India. The only part of Jammu and Kashmir under foreign occupation is the part Pakistan holds, which we again call upon it to vacate," Tyagi said."India is home to one of the largest Muslim populations in the world and our minorities vote, legislate, sit on a highest court and lead our institutions. In Pakistan, Hindu, Sikh and Christian communities have shrunk drastically since independence. Their daughters are abducted, forcibly converted and married off.Blasphemy laws hang over every minority household. Its own Muslim minorities, Shias, Ahmadiyyas, Ismailis and Hazaras face systemic persecution and their places of worship are attacked and desecrated," he added.Exposing this blatant double standard, Kshitij Tyagi said, "The Council does not need Pakistan to explain what happened in 1990 to the Kashmiri Pandits driven from their homes by terrorists Pakistan armed, trained and sent across the border.""Those same terrorists have since killed Kashmiris of every faith, many of them Muslim. The State that sponsored them is now asking this Council for an inquiry. The irony will not be lost on this Council," he added.Meanwhile, ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal issued a stern rejection of a letter circulated by Pakistan to the UN Security Council concerning a Court of Arbitration pronouncement on the Indus Waters Treaty, castigating Islamabad for twisting international legal mechanisms.Exposing Pakistan's systemic falsehoods, Randhir Jaiswal stated, "Regarding the 'permanent court' or so-called 'Permanent Court of Arbitration', I would like to say that Pakistan has a habit of misrepresenting facts and propagating falsehoods to serve its malicious propaganda."Reiterating India's principled and unyielding legal position, Randhir Jaiswal added, "For starters, the so-called ruling is not a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration as sought to be projected by the Pakistan minister. It is a ruling by an illegally-constituted court. We see this as just another attempt by Pakistan at distorting reality. Our position on this issue is very clear and we have reiterated it several times. "

India calls out Islamabad for its illegal occupation of parts of Jammu and Kashmir and demanding that it vacate them. India rejects letter circulated by Pakistan to UN Security Council concerning a Court of Arbitration pronouncement on Indus Waters Treaty.

Article Title: SC seeks timeframe from EC on deciding TMC factional feud
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Observing that the dispute between two rival factions of All India Trinamool Congress claiming the party name and symbol should be adjudicated within reasonable time, Supreme Court on Thursday asked the Election Commission to give a timeframe to decide the matter.While hearing a plea filed by former CM Mamata Banerjee challenging EC's interim order freezing the party symbol, a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said early adjudication was desirable and the poll panel could conduct day-to-day hearings. "We have seen what delay does in the Shiv Sena (factional dispute) case," the bench said.Appearing for Banerjee, advocate Kapil Sibal said he was not seeking a stay on EC's interim order as bypolls had commenced. The bench said it could not touch the order during the election process.Sibal, however, questioned the Election Commission's intention in passing the interim order during elections, saying it left his client without a remedy, and sought a final order by the end of Oct. He argued that no reason was given for the interim order and no prima facie view was taken. Sibal said the order could have been passed before the election, when his client would have had a remedy.Mamata and Ritabrata factions are at loggerheads, claiming to be the original party. Senior advocates Mukul Rohatgi and N K Kaul, for the rival faction, told the bench that EC should be given breathing space. They said a one-month period was too short to decide the issue as it would require submission of affidavits and evidence.The court asked EC's counsel Dama Seshadri Naidu to take instructions on how much time it would take to decide the dispute, and brief the court. "Find out, for final adjudication, how much time are you expected to take? A reasonable time in which parties are given fair opportunity and you have time to apply your mind... but not too long," the bench told him and posted the case for Sept 28.
Article Summary: Mamata and Ritabrata factions are at loggerheads, claiming to be the original party. The court asked EC's counsel Dama Seshadri Naidu to take instructions on how much time it would take to decide the dispute.

Article Title: EC may order SSR of rolls in Oct for poll-bound states
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission is likely to order the special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in the poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur in October, with January 1, 2027 as the qualifying date. However, it is unlikely to go for a nationwide special summary revision this year in view of special intensive revision (SIR) Phase 3 currently underway in 19 states/UTs and the ongoing census exercise.As per media reports, election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi are said to have objected to non-conduct of a nationwide SSR after 01.01.2025 1- an issue also amplified by Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi at his press conference on Thursday. However, the sources explained that this was because SIR was underway towards the end of 2025 in a dozen states including poll-bound West Bengal, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Assam (special summary revision) and Puducherry, and had been completed only a few months back in Bihar. Besides, EC was already planning to conduct the third phase of SIR covering 19 states/UTs in 2026. The commission had to be equally mindful of the census exercise, the first phase was scheduled between April 1, 2026 and Sept 30, 2026.The second phase of census is already underway in a Ladakh and the snow-bound areas of J&K, Himachal Pradesh andUttarakhand and has been preponed in the states due for assembly polls early next year. For the rest of the country, it will follow in February 2027.The special summary revision of electoral rolls in the poll-bound states later this year will be in accordance with Section 21 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950 that mandates roll revision with reference to the qualifying date before each general election to the House of the People or to the legislative assembly or a bye-election. Since the elections in the five states are to be held in February-March 2027, the updated rolls will have to be published in early January.As for the other states and UTs, sources cited sub-section 2(b) of Section 21 of R P Act, which states that revision of electoral roll every year is not mandatory and shall be revised by reference to the qualifying date "if such revision has been directed by EC".“Both SSR and SIR are done under Section 21 of RP Act 1950 and are optional. There is no legal requirement to hold both together,” an EC official told TOI.Sources said since immediate polls are not imminent in these states, there is no urgency to hold SSR. This, however, would not prevent anyone who turns 18 during this interim period, from enrolling by filling up Form 6, said an EC official.“As per the Amendment in Section 14 of RP Act 1950 in 2021 read with Section 19 of RP Act 1950, any person whose name in not on the electoral rolls or attains 18 years of age on Jan 1, 1 April 1, a July 1 or Oct 1 can register as a voter without waiting for any kind of revision as a part of regular updation of electoral rolls,” said the officer.EC is likely to wait until after the census to conduct SSR in states/UTs other than the poll-bound ones. This is essentially because the same set of field officers are involved in the roll revision and census enumeration."After SIR is completed, there has to be a reasonable period -- like a year of so -- before the next SSR is ordered as booth level officers cannot be engaged in perpetuity."
Article Summary: The Election Commission is likely to order the special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in the poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Goa and Manipur in October. January 1, 2027 is the qualifying date. However, it is unlikely to go for a nationwide special summary revise this year in view of special intensive revision (SIR) Phase 3 currently underway in 19 states/UTs.

Article Title: 'No eligible elector will be left behind': Goa CEO clarifies on 97 missing voters
Article Text:

What happened to 97 voters

NEW DELHI: The Office of the Chief Electoral Officer of Goa on Thursday clarified the controversy surrounding 97 voters who were not included in the final electoral roll published in February 2026, saying the cases were subsequently processed through house-to-house visits and that many of the voters have since been enrolled.In a press note shared on X, the CEO's office said the 97 cases were separately processed by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for completion of Form 6, the application used for inclusion of names in the electoral roll."Many have since been enrolled, while the remaining cases are being processed," the office said, adding that no eligible elector would be left out.The clarification comes amid a controversy over the exclusion of the 97 voters following Goa's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.According to an Indian Express report, the 97 voters had initially been flagged during the SIR process for what the Election Commission described as "logical discrepancies" in the electoral database.These discrepancies could arise from issues such as mismatches while linking an elector to parents or grandparents in older electoral rolls.The affected voters were subsequently given an opportunity to submit documents and objections.In Goa, 649 electors came forward, following which Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant EROs examined their cases. Officials found 97 cases where the earlier decisions needed to be reversed and the voters were eligible for inclusion.However, the final electoral roll published on February 21, 2026, did not include the 97 names.The issue subsequently drew attention to the Election Commission's ECINet electoral-roll software.According to an Indian Express investigation, the Goa CEO's office sent eight communications between February 11 and 17 seeking a rollback or reversion facility that would allow the earlier deletion decisions to be reversed.The controversy has also triggered criticism from opposition parties, which have questioned the functioning and centralisation of the electoral-roll system.
Article Summary: 97 voters were not included in the final electoral roll published in February 2026. The cases were subsequently processed through house-to-house visits. Many of the voters have since been enrolled, the Chief Electoral Officer of Goa said. The clarification comes amid a controversy over the exclusion of the 97 voters.

DEHRADUN: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami on Thursday flagged off four successful mountaineering expeditions conducted by the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering (NIM) in Uttarkashi, at the Chief Minister's Camp Office in Dehradun.The expeditions included a joint Mount Aconcagua expedition carried out in collaboration with the Jawahar Institute of Mountaineering and Winter Sports (JIM&WS), Pahalgam.Congratulating the mountaineers on the successful completion of their expeditions, CM Dhami appreciated their courage, discipline, technical expertise and team spirit displayed during challenging high-altitude conditions.He said that the achievements of the mountaineers would inspire the youth of Uttarakhand and across the country to take up adventure activities.Furthermore, CM Dhami also inaugurated the newly constructed gaushala at Haldi Farm in Khatima, Udham Singh Nagar.Addressing the gathering, he added, "Today's event is not merely the formal inauguration of a 'gaushala', where a shelter is built, opened, and we all gather and leave, but rather a symbol of our resolve to provide a safe and dignified home for all the destitute cattle that have no one to look after them and are currently roaming the streets.That initiative begins here today. I am aware that for some time now, our farmer brothers and sisters have been deeply troubled by these stray cattle roaming freely. .. If a fence weakened even slightly, the crops would be wiped out... Above all, the animals themselves were unsafe... However, I am fully confident that the opening of this magnificent gaushala will bring great relief to our farmers and residents regarding this issue..."Speaking to reporters, CM Dhami said, "A shelter has been established here for more than 2000 destitute cattle. This initiative will expand further; we are constructing similar 'gaushalas' (cow shelters) at over 60 locations across the state to address the issue of stray cattle roaming the streets-a situation that poses risks to the animals themselves and causes significant trouble for farmers and the general public, including the destruction of crops.He added, "Therefore, they deserve a dignified place to stay, along with proper arrangements for fodder and other necessities. We have put all the required systems in place and have also called upon voluntary organisations to step forward and contribute to this cause. The completion of this 'gaushala' marks significant progress in our efforts, and I hope that, with everyone's cooperation, our work will continue to advance in the same manner. "
Article Summary: Uttarakhand chief minister Pushkar Singh Dhami flagged off four successful mountaineering expeditions conducted by the Nehru Institute of Mountaineering (NIM) in Uttarkashi. He also inaugurated the newly constructed gaushala at Haldi Farm in Khatima.

Article Title: EC faultlines have a long history, dating back to 1989
Article Text:
Election Commission of India

Poll Vote & Share your view Which internal conflict within the Election Commission do you find most concerning? Seshan vs. Gill and Krishnamurthy Gopalaswami vs. Chawla Arora vs. Lavasa Goyal's resignation 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: It is not the first time that the fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989.Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner (CEC) R V S Peri Sastri. Though Sastri never publicly spoke about it, it is widely believed that the new arrangement was perceived by him as a dilution in power. By January 1990, the appointment of the two commissioners was rescinded and the EC reverted to being a single—member body.In 1993, with T N Seshan as an all-powerful CEC, the commission was once again made a multi-member body with the appointment of election commissioners M S Gill and G V G Krishnamurthy. What followed was a running feud between Seshan on the one hand and Gill and Krishnamurthy on the other. Seshan viewed the appointments as a direct assault on the independence of his office and completely refused to recognize the two new commissioners. He refused to share official documents with Gill and Krishnamurthy, barred them from attending critical meetings, and would not allocate them any office work. He openly ridiculed the election commissioners in interviews, even referring to them as “two donkeys in my office”.Interestingly, it was on Seshan’s plea challenging the govt’s decision to make EC a multi-member body that the Supreme Court had, in 1995, ruled that the election commissioners and CEC were equal in status, power and decision-making authority and that the CEC was only “first among equals”.The other internal feud in EC to recall would be one between then CEC N Gopalaswami and election commissioner Navin Chawla between 2006 and 2009. Months before he was to step down upon the end of his tenure, Gopalaswami wrote to the President of India recommending the removal of Chawla on grounds of a pro-Congress bias. In his note to the President, Gopalaswami alleged that Chawla was passing on details of EC’s meetings to senior Congress leaders, often taking “toilet breaks” during commission meetings to do so. Gopalaswami’s recommendation was however turned down by the Manmohan Singh govt and Chawla succeeded him as CEC.During the 2019 general election, the differences between then CEC Sunil Arora and then election commissioner Ashok Lavasa came to the fore, with media reports alleging that he had dissented in cases relating to complaints of alleged model code of conduct violations by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah, but was overruled without the commission making his dissent noted public. EC put out a clarification that dissent notes were only made public in quasi-judicial orders passed by EC.Lavasa resigned on August 18, 2020, two years short of his tenure, and joined the Manila-headquartered Asian Development Bank (ADB) as its Vice-President.Arun Goyal was the last election commissioner to quit in the middle of his term. Though he had cited personal reasons in his resignation dated March 9, 2024, it was widely speculated that he was not on the best of terms with the then chief election commissioner Rajiv Kumar.
Article Summary: The fault lines within the Election Commission are out in the open. The trend started from the time it became a multi-member body in 1989. Two election commissioners S S Dhanoa and V S Seigell were appointed in October 1989 and joined the poll body then led by chief election commissioner R V S Peri Sastri.

Article Title: Kalkaji gang-rape: Police probe if Aastha Kunj park was hunting ground of accused
Article Text:
The unlit road near LSR College where a police encounter with one of the accused took place Tuesda

Call detail records, CCTV footage place three accused near park at time of crime





NEW DELHI: Police investigating the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj park in south Delhi on Monday evening are trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported.They were clearly looking for a vulnerable target, say police sources, with Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - taking the lead in entering the park, followed by the two brothers, Hemant Singh and Mukesh Singh. They then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the hapless couple.Police sources said the girl and her friend were sitting on a bench around 7:15 pm when the three men allegedly approached them, posing as policemen in civvies.Having intimidated the two teenagers, they took the boy around 200m away and slapped and threatened him before taking the girl to a secluded, dark stretch of the park. That's where they took turns to allegedly rape her. The girl was threatened against disclosing the incident to anyone.She was asked to leave the place immediately. By around 8pm, the men had left the spot, police said.According to the investigators, Hemant and Mukesh went out for dinner after that and returned home later. Asif seemed to be more cautious. Police got an early lead but couldn't find him either at the Okhla mandi or his house on Monday night.The girl returned to her friend and told him what had happened. The two left the park around 8:45pm. That's when the boy made a PCR call, which brought the cops to the park. The cops are now trying to establish how Asif had procured the pistol.They claim to have found "objectionable material", including videos, on Asif's phone, sources said. Some data was allegedly deleted from the phones of Hemant and Mukesh. These have been sent to Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for retrieval.So far, the police have not come across any old complaints against the three. "We are checking whether someone may not have filed a complaint because of threats," a senior police officer said.The police are pursuing this angle because the three men would often hang around the park in the late hours. Hemant and Mukesh have allegedly changed their statements frequently during questioning. At one point, they claimed they were at home when the incident took place but gave a different account later. Their call detail records and CCTV footage, however, allegedly placed them near the park at the time.Sources said police are also investigating allegations that Hemant was removed from a gym he frequented following complaints of misbehaviour against him. The three have been sent to judicial custody for two days.DDA is facing a lot of flak for not having improved security in the park despite being alerted at least three times by the police since 2025. The police have pointed out that there were no CCTV cameras inside the park.Sources in DDA said their horticulture department had written multiple letters in the past one year to increase patrolling at the park. "Nine security guards are deployed in each shift at strategic locations, along with supervisory and patrolling arrangements. The lighting installations in the Aastha Kunj Park are functional and are inspected regularly. However, installing cameras at each spot won't be practical," a DDA official said.Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar, meanwhile, visited Aastha Kunj Park around 8.15pm Tuesday. He patrolled the park with other officers and reviewed security arrangements in and around the premises. He also directed the officers to further strengthen security through increased motorcycle and foot patrols .
Article Summary: Police trying to establish if the three accused have been involved in similar incidents earlier that have gone unreported. Asif - armed with a pistol and a condom in pocket - took the lead in entering the park. Hemant and Mukesh Singh then teamed up to unleash 40 minutes of terror on the couple.

Article Title: Lewis Hamilton put £20 million behind a promise to change Formula 1; here’s the foundation he built for motorsport’s future
Article Text:
Lewis Hamilton put £20 million behind a promise to change Formula 1; here’s the foundation he built for motorsport’s future

Why did Lewis Hamilton launch Mission 44 after looking at an F1 team photo

How did Lewis Hamilton turn that research into opportunities for Black students

What has Lewis Hamilton’s Ignite partnership done for motorsport engineering

How far has Lewis Hamilton’s Mission 44 grown since the £20 million pledge

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lewis Hamilton launched Mission 44 in July 2021 with a personal pledge of £20 million, using his success in Formula 1 to create more opportunities for young people from underrepresented backgrounds. The foundation grew from a problem Hamilton had seen throughout his racing career, the lack of Black people across motorsport, particularly in technical and engineering roles. Before launching Mission 44, he worked with the Royal Academy of Engineering on a 10-month study into those barriers. The Hamilton Commission later produced 10 recommendations, giving Hamilton a research-based plan for turning concern about representation into action.The idea did not start with a new charity. It started with Hamilton looking at an end-of-season Formula 1 photograph in 2019 and noticing how few Black faces were in it. The problem was bigger than the 20 drivers who compete in F1. Hamilton was looking at the thousands of people who design cars, build parts, work in factories, handle data and support teams away from the cameras.The Hamilton Commission was created with the Royal Academy of Engineering to understand why Black people were so underrepresented in British motorsport.Its report, “Accelerating Change: Improving Representation of Black People in UK Motorsport”, was published in July 2021 after 10 months of research. It looked at education, university admissions, apprenticeships, recruitment and workplace culture rather than treating the issue as something that started when a person applied for an F1 job.The report found that the UK motorsport sector employed about 40,000 people, while estimates from interviews suggested that less than 1% of people working in Formula 1 came from Black backgrounds. It also found that F1 teams often recruited engineering graduates from Russell Group universities, creating another barrier because Black engineering students were not spread evenly across those institutions.One figure showed just how early the problem could begin. In 2019, only two Black Caribbean students in the whole of England achieved an A* in A-level physics. The report also found that just over 3,800 Black students were studying engineering across UK universities, with about 820 at Russell Group universities.Hamilton did not limit the response to racing teams. Mission 44 looked at the education pipeline first, because a person cannot enter an engineering job in motorsport if they have already been pushed away from science and maths years earlier.One early partnership was with Teach First. In October 2021, Mission 44 announced a two-year programme aimed at recruiting and training 150 Black STEM teachers for schools serving disadvantaged communities in England. The programme also included mentoring, research, networking and other efforts to understand how more Black graduates could be encouraged into STEM teaching.That approach connected directly to one of the Hamilton Commission’s findings. The report said Black Caribbean pupils were less likely to be placed in higher science sets and highlighted concerns around teacher expectations, school behaviour policies and access to science subjects. It also found that fewer than 10 Black students were studying motorsport qualifications in further education in 2019/20.Mission 44 also moved closer to motorsport itself. Through the Ignite partnership with Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team, more than £5 million in seed funding was made available for projects designed to improve diversity and inclusion in motorsport. The partnership supported programmes ranging from grassroots participation to specialist engineering education.One of the clearest examples is the motorsport engineering scholarship programme run with the Royal Academy of Engineering. The scheme was created after the Hamilton Commission identified the gap between Black students studying engineering and their chances of moving into motorsport.The first scholarship cohort was announced in 2023, with five students from Black or mixed Black backgrounds receiving financial and career support for motorsport-related master’s degrees. The programme has since expanded. In the 2024/25 period, eight new students received scholarships, with each getting a £28,000 grant alongside career development support.The programme is still developing. In January 2026, Mission 44 and the Royal Academy of Engineering announced an expanded version of the MSc Motorsport Scholarship. The new scheme offers scholarships worth up to £43,000 and is open to a wider group of candidates.Ignite also backed programmes outside engineering. Its first grants included support for Motorsport UK’s work to increase female participation in grassroots motorsport, showing that the partnership was not built around one route into the sport.Mission 44 has since moved beyond its original focus on British motorsport. Its latest annual report says the foundation reached 550,000 young people during 2024/25 and expanded its work in the United States. It also launched an education policy campaign and continued funding organisations working on education and STEM access.That change is crucial because Hamilton’s original concern was never only about finding another Black Formula 1 driver. The Hamilton Commission showed that the barriers could appear much earlier, from school subject choices to access to technical education, university pathways and professional networks.The numbers also explain why Hamilton chose to build a foundation rather than simply make a one-time donation. The problem was spread across several stages of a young person’s life. Mission 44’s work has therefore included teachers, schools, engineering students, grassroots programmes and routes into employment.Five years after the £20 million pledge, the most visible part of Hamilton’s work is no longer just the amount of money attached to it. There is now a continuing structure behind the idea, research to identify barriers, partnerships to address them and scholarships and programmes designed to help young people move through the pipeline.The original photograph gave Hamilton a question. The Hamilton Commission helped define the problem, and Mission 44 became the vehicle for acting on it. In 2026, that work is still expanding, with the motorsport scholarship programme itself moving into a larger phase.
Article Summary: Lewis Hamilton launched Mission 44 in July 2021 with a personal pledge of £20 million. The foundation grew from a problem Hamilton had seen throughout his racing career, the lack of Black people across motorsport. The Hamilton Commission was created with the Royal Academy of Engineering to understand why Black people were so underrepresented in British motorsports. Mission 44 announced a two-year programme aimed at recruiting 150 Black STEM teachers.

Article Title: Who is Suruchi Singh? 19-year-old with 5 World Cup golds in one season goes from 26th in 10m air pistol individuals to Asian Games gold in mixed

Suruchi Singh, left, and Kamaljeet celebrate after winning Gold medal in the 10 meter air pistol mixed team final (PTI Photo)

From Jhajjar’s fields to the shooting range

The ritual before every big match

Asian Games gold completes another breakthrough

Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won the maiden gold medal in shooting for India at the Asian Games 2026 after a stunning performance in the mixed team event.Kamaljeet and Suruchi shot a total of 484.6 in the final. They were followed by South Korea’s Suhyeon Hong and Gaeun Choo, who finished second with 478.0. The Korean pair were 6.6 points behind Kamaljeet and Suruchi, underlining the Indian duo’s dominance in the final.Iran bagged the bronze medal with 415.8.But Suruchi’s journey to the Asian Games gold medal was far from easy. The 19-year-old comes from a humble family in Haryana, and when TimesofIndia.com spoke to her coach Suresh Singh last year, he recalled how he agreed to train her, but only after laying down his own conditions.Born in Jhajjar, Haryana, Suruchi comes from a humble family. Her coach, Suresh Singh, has previously recalled how the youngster remains closely connected to her roots, helping with work at home and even operating farm machinery.“If she weren’t at the World Cup today, she’d be home harvesting wheat,” Suresh had told TOI.When Suruchi and her father, Inder Singh, first met the coach, her father made his priority clear: he wanted his daughter to learn discipline alongside the sport.Suresh agreed to take her on, but with a condition, Suruchi would have to follow his system rather than simply focus on pulling the trigger.That decision changed her career.Suruchi won medals at the 2022 and 2023 Nationals before producing a spectacular breakthrough in 2024, when she won seven gold medals at the National Championships in Delhi. She followed that up with two more gold medals at the National Games in Uttarakhand.In 2025, Suruchi began making headlines on the ISSF World Cup circuit, winning individual gold medals in Lima, Buenos Aires and Munich.Despite her international success, Suruchi has retained one habit that keeps her connected to the person who helped shape her career. Before a competition, she calls her coach. Even at major international events, she would contact Suresh minutes before stepping onto the range.“Sir, I have five minutes before I go in, what should I do?” she would ask.The Asian Games gold also reflected the mentality Suruchi has developed through years of training. If she decides to fire 150 shots during a training session and the final shot does not land where she wants it to, Suruchi does not simply pack up and leave. She keeps shooting until she gets the result she wants.The road to Friday’s gold had not been entirely smooth. Suruchi finished 26th in the women’s individual 10m air pistol qualification at the Asian Games, while India also missed out on a medal in the women’s team event.But the mixed team event offered another opportunity.Suruchi and Kamaljeet seized it. They topped the qualification before carrying that momentum into the final. Their 484.6 points gave them a clear advantage over South Korea and secured India’s maiden gold medal at the Asian Games 2026.
Article Summary: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won the maiden gold medal in shooting for India at the Asian Games 2026 after a stunning performance in the mixed team event. The 19-year-old comes from a humble family in Haryana. Suruchi won medals at the 2022 and 2023 Nationals before producing a spectacular breakthrough in 2024.

Article Title: Was Travis Kelce's grandfather a Russian spy? The 1980s controversial case and the truth behind his family mystery explained
Article Text:
Travis Kelce (Image via Getty)

Was Travis Kelce’s grandfather involved in Russian espionage?

What Jason Kelce and Donna Kelce revealed about their grandfather

New Heights

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A resurfaced video of Travis Kelce, Jason Kelce discussing his grandfather’s criminal past has brought an unusual chapter of the former Philadelphia Eagles star’s family history back into the spotlight. The story sounds like something out of a spy thriller, with Soviet business ties, stolen industrial designs and criminal charges. But was Kelce’s grandfather really a Russian spy, or has the story taken on a life of its own? The answer is more complex than the rumours suggest. While the case involved dealings with a Soviet company, the charges had nothing to do with treason or spying for Russia.The controversy dates back to the early 1980s and centres on Donald Roy Blalock, Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce’s maternal grandfather. Blalock spent years working in the Soviet Union as a salesman for C-E Cast Equipment Co., a Cleveland-based manufacturer.After returning to the United States, he left the company and joined a competitor. The move raised concerns when C-E Cast noticed a sharp drop in Soviet sales. An investigation later led authorities to accuse Blalock and three former colleagues of stealing confidential blueprints and using them to produce competing machine parts.Prosecutors alleged that Blalock used the alias Bob Steele and sold more than $500,000 worth of parts, many to a Soviet truck manufacturer. The case involved industrial espionage allegations, but it was not a case of Blalock acting as a Russian intelligence agent.Court records showed that Blalock faced charges including conversion of trade secrets and receiving stolen property. In 1984, he pleaded guilty to a lesser misdemeanor charge involving stolen property worth less than $150. He received a suspended one-year probation sentence and had to pay $10,000 in restitution.The resurfaced video brings renewed attention to Travis Kelce and Jason Kelce’s conversation with their mother, Donna Kelce, onin 2023. Jason raised the family mystery with a blunt question: “Was grandpa actually charged with treason?”Jason later admitted he did not know the full details, saying: “I don’t know if he was actually helping out Russia or what the full level of that was. It was definitely shady.”Donna pushed back against the idea that her father sold secrets to a foreign power. She said: “He was stealing plans that they had already thrown in the trash,” before adding, “He wasn’t selling secrets to the CIA or Russia. ... The worst thing that happened was that he had his pension taken away. That was about it.”Despite the criminal case, Blalock’s legacy within the family was not entirely defined by the controversy. Donna described her father as flawed, while also recalling moments when he showed generosity and support.Jason Kelce even encouraged Jason’s football ambitions with a card bearing the words “press on!” Reflecting on that influence, Jason offered a nuanced view of his grandfather: “He wasn’t a great grandpa but he was a great grandpa in the right moment.”Ultimately, the records support a case involving stolen property and business secrets, not treason or confirmed Russian spying.
Article Summary: The controversy centres on Donald Roy Blalock, Jason Kelce and Travis Kelce’s maternal grandfather. The case involved industrial espionage allegations, but it was not a case of Russian spying. In 1984, he pleaded guilty to a lesser misdemeanor charge involving stolen property worth less than $150.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: India one step away from defending kabaddi gold medals as men and women storm into finals

India eye kabaddi double

India’s kabaddi team continued their dominance at the Asian Games 2026 as both the men’s and women’s teams secured their places in the gold-medal matches with semifinal victories. The women’s side defeated Nepal 48-24, while the men’s team followed with an emphatic 66-27 win over Thailand. The results ensured that India will have a chance to defend both kabaddi titles at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.For the women, the victory kept alive their bid for a fourth consecutive Asian Games gold medal. India have won the women’s kabaddi title at every Asian Games since the sport was introduced to the women’s programme in 2010.The Indian women established control early and went into the interval with a 31-17 advantage. India combined successful raids with a disciplined defensive effort and repeatedly put Nepal under pressure. The four all-outs in the opening half gave the defending champions a substantial cushion.Nepal struggled to match India's intensity after the break. They managed only seven points in the second half as India maintained their advantage and eventually completed a 24-point victory.The win extended India's unbeaten run in the competition. They had previously defeated Iran, Bangladesh and Japan during the group stage. The defending champions will now turn their attention to the final, where they will look to maintain their remarkable record in the women's event.The men's team delivered an equally commanding performance against Thailand. India raced into an early lead and were comfortably ahead at 37-18 at half-time. Thailand showed flashes of resistance, with Theeradat Chaisit producing a strong spell in attack, but India quickly regained control.The Indian side continued to pile on the points after the break and eventually crossed the 50-point mark. Thailand could not keep pace with India's raiders and defenders as the gap continued to widen. India eventually closed out the semifinal with a 66-27 victory.The two semifinal victories mean India are now guaranteed medals in both kabaddi competitions. The women's team are chasing a fourth successive gold, while the men are aiming to retain the title they won at the previous Asian Games.India have historically dominated men's kabaddi at the Asian Games, having won eight gold medals since the sport made its debut in 1990. Iran are the only other nation to have won the men's title, doing so in 2018 when India had to settle for bronze.The Indian teams will now have one final hurdle to clear in Nagoya.

Article Title: 'Final mein gai, to gold hi layegi': Suruchi Inder Singh's coach after Asian Games 2026 triumph
Article Text:
Suruchi and her teammate Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team event (Image credit: Agencies)

Suruchi's gold-winning show

Hours of work before the Asian Games

NEW DELHI: “Final mein gayi, to gold hi layegi,” an elated Suresh Singh said after his student Suruchi Inder Singh helped India win its first gold medal of the day at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Friday.Suruchi and her teammate Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team event, finishing on top at the Aichi General Shooting Range to give India its second gold medal of the Games.For Suruchi, the victory came after a disappointing individual event.The Haryana shooter, who won four individual World Cup gold medals in 2025 in Buenos Aires, Munich, Lima and Doha, including the World Cup Final, failed to qualify for the final in the individual 10m air pistol event. In a field of 55 shooters, she finished 26th in qualification with a score of 568-12x.“She was disappointed. But I knew she would come back stronger. She knows how to bounce back quickly, and that is her best quality. The moment she reached the final, I was 200 percent sure that she would win gold. That’s how she is,” the coach said.Suruchi and Kamaljeet were in control from the start of the mixed team final. The pair scored 103.0 in the first series of Stage 1, followed by 202.4 and 303.5.They continued their strong performance in Stage 2, scoring 364.7 in the first series and staying comfortably ahead of South Korea and Iran.After 18 shots, India remained at the top and extended their lead with a score of 424.9 in the second series of Stage 2.Suruchi and Kamaljeet eventually finished with a total score of 484.6 to win the gold medal.South Korea's Suhyeon Hong and Gaeun Choo finished second with 478.0. The Korean pair were 6.6 points behind the Indians, underlining India's control of the final.“She is an athlete for the finals. Look at her past record. If she has reached the final, then you can't stop her. She will go for gold. She doesn't want silver or bronze. She has that kind of hunger,” Suresh said.Ahead of the Asian Games, Suruchi worked on several aspects of her shooting with Suresh at his Guru Dronacharya Shooting Academy in Bhiwani.The coach said they focused on her technique, holding and dry-fire training. Suruchi's father had initially wanted her to take up wrestling.“She worked on her holding and did dry-fire training for hours to improve her focus. We also worked on some technical aspects,” he said.One of the key areas they focused on was timing.“The most important focus was on timing. I am a coach who focuses on timing and wants my shooter to finish the match early. I told the same thing to Suruchi. We used to decide a particular time and try to finish the shot within that time.“For example, if you have 60 seconds for one shot, finish that shot early. It helps you take the pressure off yourself and allows you to focus,” he said.Now, Suresh is waiting to welcome his student home.“I am just waiting for her. She has made everyone proud. We are eagerly waiting to welcome her,” the coach said.
Article Summary: Suruchi Inder Singh helped India win its first gold medal of the day at the Asian Games 2026 in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, on Friday. Suruchi and her teammate Kamaljeet won gold in the 10m air pistol mixed team event.

Article Title: 'Staying home can’t be our safety policy', women take to the streets in Delhi
Article Text:
'There is a pink booth near the back gate road, but it’s always empty. Now we are being told by the authorities that someone will be there always, but it’s sad that it takes a bad crime to happen for this to be taken seriously,' says Aarya, a third year Journalism student (Pic: @du_beat)

Reached? – The question women’s

safety

begins and ends with

'Police commissioner had a meeting with us in the auditorium Thursday morning, sharing safety precautions with us. There has been police deployment since Tuesday, but let’s see if it helps the safety issue. The back gate is always secluded and unsafe, we never take this route alone,' shares Gudia, second year Hindi student, who lives near Badarpur (Pic: @du_beat)

- As told to Sara Siddiqui





Anusha Garg, a third-year journalism student and President of the LSR Students’ Union, expresses what every woman occupying public spaces in Delhi feels:This week, after a minor was reportedly gang- raped in a South Delhi, my first instinct was: safety had to come first. But I kept returning to the one contradiction – the danger was outside, yet we were the ones being asked to retreat.Women’s safety is not something we discuss only after a disturbing headline. It is built into our everyday plans. Among friends, “reached?” is almost a form of punctuation. If a college event ends late, the conversation changes quickly, “Metro or cab? Is that road crowded? Should we leave together? Share your location. Call when you reach”. These calculations become so routine that we barely register them. But there is a thin line between protection and restriction. “Come home early” can become the answer to a problem women did not create.National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data show that 13,396 crimes against women were registered in Delhi in 2024. Registered crime is not the same as the full prevalence of violence, but the figure makes it impossible to dismiss the anxiety women carry through the city.And that anxiety has a cost.A spontaneous evening out for a male friend comes with logistical queries for us: route, transport, company, phone battery, one last message home. “Stay home” cannot be our final safety policy. If women withdraw whenever public spaces feel unsafe, those spaces do not become safer; they simply become devoid of women. I will still share my location. I will still text “reached”. Precautions matter. But a safe city cannot be one where women become experts at disappearing. It has to be one where our presence requires no explanation.
Article Summary: Women’s safety is not something we discuss only after a disturbing headline. It is built into our everyday plans. Among friends, “reached?” is almost a form of punctuation. National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) data show that 13,396 crimes against women were registered in Delhi in 2024.

Article Title: Gyanesh Kumar: Himanta defends Gyanesh Kumar amid ECI ‘dissent’ row
Article Text:
The Indian Express

The Indian Express





Guwahati: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Thursday asserted that the chief election commissioner (CEC) cannot take decisions without consulting the other election commissioners, defending CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid the political storm over reported dissent within the Election Commission of India (ECI).The row follows a Wednesday report by, which claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times over roughly 10 months to SIR-related decisions, including voter deletions and electoral roll data. The Commission, however, has said that decisions relating to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) were taken unanimously with the approval of all three commissioners.At a press conference here, when asked for his reaction to the report, Sarma said that the CEC was being targeted as part of a “political campaign,” which he said reflected the “frustration” of the Opposition and “dimagi” (intellectual) Naxals.“The election commission is a three-member body, and any decision requires the signatures of all three members,” he said, noting that had two commissioners genuinely opposed the CEC on a final decision, the outcome would have gone against him in a 2-1 vote.Drawing a parallel with cabinet functioning, Sarma said it was routine for different officials to record differing views before a final call is made. “Before a decision is taken on a file, different officials may record different views. The same happens in the cabinet. A deputy secretary may make one observation, a joint secretary another, and ultimately the cabinet discusses the matter and takes a decision,” he said.He characterised the episode reported byas “pre-decision-making consultation” rather than evidence of a rift, adding that the Commission’s three members “sit together and take the decision,” and that nothing counts as an ECI decision unless all three sign off.“I therefore do not think there is much controversy in this matter, particularly because the Election Commission itself has provided a clarification on the issue,” Sarma said, suggesting the report was “published mainly to create a sensation.”He maintained that the EC functions as a collective body and that all decisions carry the signatures of the CEC and both election commissioners.“Those who know Election Commission rules won’t level such an allegation. In my humble view, the EC cannot take any decision when the CEC or the election commissioners are in a minority. All EC decisions have to be passed or taken in majority as a collective body,” Sarma said.
Article Summary: Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma defends CEC Gyanesh Kumar amid political storm over reported dissent within the Election Commission of India. The row follows a Wednesday report by, which claimed that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected at least 14 times over roughly 10 months to SIR-related decisions.

A safer route, with precautions

Beyond College Gate, How Safe Are Roads Just Outside?

Article Title: Gurgaon road rage: 4 men smash car window, then attack complainants outside police station
Article Text:
Four men allegedly got out of the SUV and tried to open his car door.





GURGAON: Four men allegedly intercepted a car and smashed its window on Thursday before attacking the complainant and two of his associates outside New Colony police station, where they had gone to lodge a complaint about the incident.The complainant, Gautam, a resident of Madanpuri, told police he was driving towards New Colony after taking a U-turn near Hari’s Bakery when a Scorpio N (HR26FG5726) overtook his car and forced him to stop.Four men allegedly got out of the SUV and tried to open his car door. When they failed, they allegedly smashed the window, and the broken glass hit Gautam’s face. He told police he suspected the men had come to rob him and were carrying illegal weapons.Gautam said he managed to drive away and called his friends Ravindra Kataria and Sandeep Dahiya. The three then went to New Colony police station to lodge a complaint. Gautam told police that a dashcam in his car had recorded the incident.Police said an emergency response vehicle received information about the incident near Aryan Hospital in Sector 7. A team reached the spot and found Gautam, Ravindra and Sandeep there, but the Scorpio had left.Police later found the SUV parked near Sai Temple at New Colony turn. Gautam told police its occupants had entered a hotel opposite the spot. A police team went to the hotel and found three men — Ajay , Mohit and Piyush Bhardwaj — in room 105. Police said the three had consumed alcohol and took them into custody.A fourth man, identified as Shivam, was apprehended while allegedly fighting with Gautam and his friends near the police station.Police said that after getting out of the police vehicle, Mohit joined Shivam and allegedly attacked Gautam, Ravindra and Sandeep near the station gate. Police personnel intervened and all four accused were taken for medical examination at Sector 10 govt hospital.Ravindra and Sandeep were also medically examined. Their reports recorded five and two injuries, respectively. Gautam also alleged that Ravindra’s gold chain went missing during the assault and that the accused threatened to kill them if they encountered them elsewhere.An FIR was registered at New Colony police station under sections 115(2), 126(2), 324(4), 351(3), 3(5) and 72(C) of Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.
Article Summary: Four men allegedly intercepted a car and smashed its window on Thursday. They then allegedly attacked the complainant and two of his associates outside New Colony police station, where they had gone to lodge a complaint about the incident. The complainant, Gautam, a resident of Madanpuri, told police he suspected the men had come to rob him.

Article Title: Ali Ghodsi CEO of world's one of the fastest-growing software company, says that key to making Databricks grow is to make sure he is not stuck in rooms with ...
Article Text:
Databricks CEO: ‘I try to compress the calendar’

Why he avoids back-to-back meetings

Part of a broader executive pushback on meeting culture

With a valuation of $190 billion, Databricks has become one of Silicon Valley’s fastest-growing software companies. But CEO Ali Ghodsi says the secret to scaling the company isn’t more meetings — it’s fewer. According to a report by Fortune, speaking on the Long Strange Trip podcast, Ghodsi explained that compressing his calendar and avoiding back-to-back sessions helps him focus on the company’s biggest challenges. Ghodsi further added that he makes sure that the top talent at his company is not suck conference room all day. Ghodsi revealed that at 8 a.m. every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, he and his team meet to identify the “main thing” — the biggest bottleneck facing Databricks. “I want to unblock that big thing that I think is going to get us 10x,” he said. Beyond those sessions, he avoids filling his calendar with meetings, warning that endless back-to-back schedules leave him “a slave to my calendar” and distracted by “monkeys on my back.”Speaking on a recent episode of the Long Strange Trip podcast, Ghodsi explained that his approach involves intentionally avoiding filling up his schedule, even though it inevitably ends up busy anyway.The goal, he said, is to preserve open blocks of time so he can keep returning to what he calls the company's "main thing" — the single biggest bottleneck standing in the way of major growth.To identify that priority, Ghodsi said he and his team meet every Monday, Wednesday, and Friday at 8 a.m. to pin down exactly what that blocking issue is and figure out how to work through it together, with the explicit goal of unblocking whatever he believes could drive 10x growth for the company.Beyond those recurring sessions, Ghodsi said he actively resists letting his calendar fill up with additional meetings. He described days packed with back-to-back sessions from morning until evening as days where he's effectively lost control of his own schedule, spending his time working through everyone else's priorities rather than his own — a dynamic he bluntly likened to carrying "monkeys on his back."Ghodsi's comments reflect a growing sentiment among top executives who argue that meeting-heavy calendars often get in the way of real progress, even as companies face constant pressure to move faster. The data backs up some of that frustration: a 2024 survey by Atlassian found that nearly three out of four meetings fail to effectively communicate information, and 77% of respondents said meetings tend to simply generate even more meetings.This skepticism isn't limited to leaders at younger companies like Databricks. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon has been especially blunt about his disdain for unnecessary meetings, famously writing "Kill meetings" in his 2024 letter to shareholders. That said, Dimon has been careful to note that not every meeting is a waste of time — he simply expects the ones that do happen to be treated with real focus and preparation. Speaking at Fortune's 2025 Most Powerful Women summit, Dimon said he always comes to meetings having done the necessary pre-reading, and expects full attention in return, saying he has no patience for attendees nodding off, checking email, or getting distracted by notifications during a meeting, calling that kind of behavior simply disrespectful.Other executives have voiced similar preferences for leaner, more conversational meetings over slide-heavy presentations, favoring direct discussion over sitting through decks read aloud.
Article Summary: Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi says the secret to scaling the company isn't more meetings, it's fewer. He says he compresses his calendar and avoids back-to-back sessions so he can focus on the company's biggest challenges. His comments reflect a growing sentiment among top executives that meeting-heavy calendars often get in the way of real progress.

Article Title: “Three-against-one situation”: El Rubius opens up on being “targeted” in MrBeast’s viral $1M challenge
Article Text:
El Rubius reacted honestly after his elimination from MrBeast’s $1 million challenge, calling it “unfair” and claiming he was targeted in a three-against-one situation. Despite his frustration, he thanked fans and gave away his $50,000 winnings. His response felt real and balanced, especially after MrBeast’s team later sent him a cake, softening the moment.

El Rubius reflects on a tough and “unfair” exit

El Rubius did not just walk away from MrBeast’s $1 million streamer challenge. He opened up. Soon after his elimination, the Spanish creator shared a raw reaction with fans, giving them a closer look at what the experience felt like from inside the game. It was not polished or carefully framed. It felt real, and that is exactly why it caught attention so quickly.The clip and his response have since fueled conversations across the streaming space. Some viewers believe intense competitions like this naturally lead to uneven situations. Others feel Rubius may have had a point about being singled out. Either way, his words have added a human layer to a challenge that many only saw as entertainment.Speaking through an Instagram Story, Rubius did not hide his frustration, but he also made sure to thank his supporters. He said, "Guys, I just got knocked out of the game. It was a bit of an unfair elimination, but hey, at least I managed to walk away with $50,000 for you all, which I’ve already distributed. It went to the mods, the subs, and the non-subs alike."He further added, "I’m happy, of course, though admittedly, it was incredibly tough.I wasn't really a fan of the challenge itself, either. But then again... it was basically a three-against-one situation the entire time. I mean, they were targeting me specifically the whole way through. I kept trying to go after RaKai, but, well, he actually just got eliminated in the end. So, at least justice was served for Abraham. Abraham, if you’re watching this, we were all rooting for you, and standing right there with you."His message carried mixed emotions. There was disappointment, yes, but also pride in how he handled things. Giving away his $50,000 winnings to his community stood out as a gesture that meant more than the result itself.He continued with another honest note, saying, "And in the end, karma finally caught up with that little punk. Sorry, I’m being a bit toxic right now, but let's just hope the MrBeast team doesn't see this! Guys, thank you all so much. Seriously, thank you for all the support and for just being there."He added, "Every time I asked for something in the chat or whatever it was, you guys were right there. You’re incredible. I’m a little disappointed in myself, personally, mostly for not performing better, but hey, I gave it my all, and we still walked away with $50,000, so we’ve got to look on the bright side. All right, guys, big hugs to all my brothers out there!"Interestingly, the story did not end with frustration. Later that day, Rubius revealed that MrBeast’s team had sent him a cake after his exit. It was a small gesture, but it shifted the mood. It showed that even in a high-pressure challenge, there is still room for respect.In the end, Rubius’ reaction felt honest and grounded. That is what stayed with people.

Article Title: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends

The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Book baithaks: Delhi's newest adda has a reading list
Article Text:
Conceptualised to create a quiet space for readers, book baithaks are very Delhi-coded, drawing from the spirit of the traditional baithak (AI Image)

Disha says, 'Baithaks encourage people to interact in a relaxed and informal setup. You add books, and more importantly stories in the mix and you have a recipe for a perfect meet-up' (Pic: @karwaanheritage)

‘Reading communities thrive on healthy conversation’

“A bookish baithak doesn’t have to be a formal literary event. It can be a gathering where literature becomes the excuse to sit together, talk deeply, and stay a little longer,” Ekta Bhandari shares (AI Image)

‘An informal setup and books make the recipe for a perfect meet-up’

I’d say these are baithaks not restricted to a theme. They are about ideas and questions that we think are relevant for our times and what we think about. These baithaks are like a sounding board for us to think out loud with people who have been working on those themes for a long time. We aim to make it feel like our college adda! Eshan Sharma, founder of an independent public history collective

Bringing together authors like Arundhati Roy and Nivedita Menon, Karwaan Baithaks is creating a space for learning, thinking and discussing in Delhi (Pic: @karwaanheritage)

‘Artistes of all kinds come together, think together, and often disagree together’

Books and baithaks are almost naturally made for each other. A baithak is fundamentally about gathering, conversation, and the exchange of ideas, and that is exactly what a good book can set in motion Ekta Bhandari, co-founder of a book club





Buying and talking about books are two of a reader’s favourite things to do, apart from reading, of course. As book clubs continue to grow, a cosy, intimate format of book events is emerging in the city. Conceptualised to create a quiet space for readers, these events are very Delhi-coded, drawing from the spirit of the traditional baithak. Think intimate gatherings, floor seating and literary discussions.Book events as a concept are a tad different from your usual Delhi hang. With quieter settings and warm lighting, connection takes over. “Book conversations and events often reflect this deep thinking, a sense of familiarity with others, and yet the openness to learning about interpretations of the material from another perspective. People in these settings are at ease, even those who may not necessarily gravitate naturally towards socialising, books presenting a great starting point for the conversations,” says Kapil Kapoor, co-founder of CMYK Bookstore.Ekta Bhandari, co-founder of Read A Kitaab, shares, “Delhi has such a rich culture of conversations around art, poetry, music, history, food and politics and books can sit beautifully at the centre of all of these.A book can become the starting point rather than the subject of the evening: you begin with a novel, and suddenly you are talking about a city, a memory, an era, an identity or something happening around you. ”Disha Verma, founder of Gurgaon’s Chapters Bookstore, notes, “I believe that the success of a book event depends on its effectiveness in generating conversations and encouraging open thinking. The air you create for people to open up matters a lot – whether it is a book club, author meet or any other engagement around stories. People need to feel safe in voicing their opinions and asking questions and extend the same generosity to others as well. Reading communities thrive on healthy conversation that can brew only in an unthreatening and intimate atmosphere.”Baithaks, which were originally focused on listening to classical music, are now being reinterpreted and explored in different formats. Talking about baithaks, Sangeeta Chopra, founder of Naadyatra Baithaks, who hosts monthly music baithaks in her home in Gurgaon, shares how books have found a space in her events, “Whenever there is a session at my house, like a listening session or a discussion on music, I put out my huge collection of books on music. If people want to browse through them, they’re most welcome to. But that happens in the following session; it’s not a part of the baithak. There’s so much variety available – autobiographies, biographies of artists, people’s interpretations of certain kinds of music, and even experiences of listening to a particular raag. There are many aspects of music that you can learn and discuss through these books.”Envisioning a book baithak, Kapil adds, “As a space, we hope to keep giving people reasons to return to the bookstore, for books, shows, and engaging conversations. For book baithaks too, the idea should be to carefully think through and curate what kind of readers/crowd one wants for each event, and how readers might experience the conversations.” Talking about the format as an intersection of books and baithaks, Disha says, “It does sound like they are a good match. Baithaks encourage people to interact in a relaxed and informal setup. You add books, and more importantly stories in the mix and you have a recipe for a perfect meet-up.”Bringing together authors like Arundhati Roy and Nivedita Menon, Karwaan Baithaks is creating a space for learning, thinking and discussing in Delhi. Eshan Sharma, founder of Karwaan Heritage that holds these baithaks, says, “All baithaks and conversations in Delhi happen around books and authors. Karwaan baithaks’ idea was to go beyond books since sometimes the events focus on book launches only. We wanted to go beyond that. Our baithaks are never tied to a particular book per se. They are curated independently, where the speaker might be an author, but the conversation goes beyond. We get artistes of all kinds, filmmakers, poets, actors, performers coming together and thinking together, often disagreeing.”
Article Summary: Book events as a concept are a tad different from your usual Delhi hang. Conceptualised to create a quiet space for readers, book baithaks are very Delhi-coded, drawing from the spirit of the traditional baithak. Think intimate gatherings, floor seating and literary discussions.

Article Title: Why does a 7pm outing need a survival strategy?
Article Text:
The responsibility for staying safe keeps being handed back to women. We are expected to anticipate danger, avoid it, document it.





At 7pm, the sky over Delhi usually settles into a dusky purple, marking an hour that should belong to anyone looking to unwind. An evening walk.A coffee with a friend. A drive home after work. For the 17-year-old girl who went to a park on her birthday evening and was reportedly gang-raped, that leisurely walk turned into a nightmare. Barely a few kilometres away, something inside me tightened into a familiar knot.An evening walk in a well-lit park should be unremarkable. Instead, my brain starts doing the calculations almost without permission. Who is walking behind me? Why has that man slowed down? Is that the quickest route back? Should I call someone? Every footstep behind me is a reason to tense up. Every man crossing my path is someone I instinctively assess before I even realise I am doing it.When returning from work every evening, the moment the door of my cab thuds shut, my first instinct is to pull out my phone and share my live location with my family. Nobody asked me to. I do it automatically, leaving a silent digital breadcrumb just in case I don’t make it to my destination.This isn’t a rant. It is fatigue.The constant preparation for something that may never happen, but that we have been taught could happen at any time.We, the women of Delhi, are tired of the quiet list of instructions that follow us everywhere. Don’t go out after dark. Don’t walk alone. Share your location. Call when you reach. Stay alert. Keep your phone charged. Be careful about what you wear. Be careful about who you trust.The responsibility for staying safe keeps being handed back to us. We are expected to anticipate danger, avoid it, document it. Meanwhile, the spaces themselves remain much the same.So perhaps the question should not only be how we can teach women to protect themselves, but why women have to be constantly taught to protect themselves in the first place.Safety cannot begin and end with a “pink police booth,” a “pink force patrolling near a school, park or metro station” or “restricted entry to parks after sunset”. It has to extend to the way public spaces are designed and monitored. Are there blind spots? Is there adequate lighting? Can a woman see who is around her? Can she get help quickly? And when someone uses real or fake authority to intimidate or harm another person, is there swift accountability?I want to reach a point where getting into a cab at 7pm does not automatically trigger the thought, “I should share my location.” Where sitting in a park does not require an assessment of every man who walks past. Where looking out of a cab window can just mean looking out of the window.The year will change. The capital will get more flyovers and metro lines. But for how many more years will women have to live with a curfew in their heads?
Article Summary: The responsibility for staying safe keeps being handed back to us. We are expected to anticipate danger, avoid it, document it. The year will change. The capital will get more flyovers and metro lines. But for how many more years will women have to live with a curfew in their heads?

Article Title: NCSC team visits IIT-B, seeks details on incident
Article Text:
Mumbai:





The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) chairman Kishor Makwana and his team visited IIT-B on Thursday and sought a comprehensive account from the officials of the sequence of events preceding Sahil Wakode’s death.“The Commission examined the circumstances in which the student was questioned during the examination, the procedure reportedly followed thereafter, the role of the concerned faculty and Institute authorities, and the institutional mechanisms available for addressing student grievances and safeguarding the welfare and rights of students belonging to Scheduled Castes,” a press release issued by the PIB said.The chairman also inspected the classroom/examination hall where the reported examination incident took place and sought information regarding the sequence of events during and immediately after the examination. The commission also asked the institute to ensure proper collection, preservation and examination of all documentary, electronic, forensic and testimonial evidence. It emphasized the need for recording the statements of students, faculty members, institute officials and others who may possess relevant information.The commission members held a meeting with senior police officials and the probe team and reviewed the status and progress of the investigation and sought details regarding the FIR, collection and preservation of evidence, CCTV footage, examination of witnesses and other relevant aspects of the case.The commission reiterated that the constitutional and statutory safeguards available to members of the Scheduled Castes must be effectively protected and that institutions must maintain appropriate mechanisms for ensuring dignity, equality, non-discrimination, student welfare and effective grievance redressal.
Article Summary: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) chairman Kishor Makwana and his team visited IIT-B on Thursday. They sought a comprehensive account from the officials of the sequence of events preceding Sahil Wakode’s death.

Article Title: ​​​Sambhajinagar gears up to bid adieu to Bappa; Greens fume over trees pruning for procession
Article Text:
Trees mercilessly pruned to make way for processions in Sutgirani chowk area

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

TOI

TOI





Ganapati mandals and households have started preparing for immersion day, marking the conclusion of the Ganeshotsav on Friday.A day before immersion, the atmosphere in the city turned enigmatic, with people feeling emotional but electric. At Ganesh mandals across the city, devotees gathered for the final darshan of Bappa as evening aartis stretched late into the night, and chants of ‘Ganapati Bappa Morya’ echoed louder and distribution of prasad reached its peak.“There was always a bittersweet mood the day before the farewell to Bappa. Like every year, the festival passed so quickly this time too amid the spirit of devotion and spirit,” said Abhishek Ranjangaokar, a youth volunteer with a Ganesh mandal.The city police have also prepared for the immersion day and announced traffic diversions on major procession routes.Environmentalists, however, were outraged after roadside trees from Garkheda Sutgirni Chowk to Jawahar Nagar Police Station have been pruned to clear the route for Ganesh immersion processions.“Branches were pruned cruelly so that 20- to 50-foot-tall idols carried on trucks and tractors face no obstruction,” Dr Kishor Pathak, an environmentalist, told. He alleged that the cutting was done on the instructions of public representatives.Pathak said Ganesh mandals were also disrespecting Lord Ganapati and inviting nature’s wrath by destroying nature.“The civic officials said that trees were being cut against their wishes due to political pressure. The private contractors cut branches in an unscientific manner despite municipal staff being present. If idols of normal height were used, there would be no obstruction of trees,” Pathak said.tried contacting Vijay Patil, garden superintendent of the civic body. He, however, could not be reached for comments by the time of going to the press.
Article Summary: Trees mercilessly pruned to make way for processions in Sutgirani chowk area. At Ganesh mandals across the city, devotees gathered for the final darshan of Bappa as evening aartis stretched late into the night.
